Prepare a combined taxonomic reference table for name matching

Source: R/prepare_taxonomic_resources.R
prepare_taxonomic_resources.Rd

Takes one or more taxonomic reference tables – loaded with load_taxonomic_resources(), built yourself, or any mix of these – and turns them into the single nested resources list that align_taxa()/match_taxa() expect: tables are combined if more than one was supplied, and the result is split by rank (and, for species-level rows, by taxonomic status). align_taxa(), update_taxa() and create_taxonomic_update_lookup() call this themselves when given a table (or a list of tables) rather than prepared resources; call it yourself to prepare once and reuse.

Usage

prepare_taxonomic_resources(
  taxonomic_resources = NULL,
  taxon_ranks_to_check = NULL
)

Arguments

taxonomic_resources

A tibble, a path to a CSV file (read with readr, which must be installed), or a (optionally named) list of either – one element per taxonomic reference table to combine. Each table must be in taxonAlign's taxonomic reference format (see taxonomic_reference_schema()): at least the columns canonical_name, scientific_name, taxon_rank, taxonomic_status, taxonomic_dataset, genus, taxon_ID and accepted_name_usage_ID, matching APCalign's own naming convention (see Details). A row whose canonical_name is NA has no usable name and is dropped, with a warning. accepted_name_usage_ID must be self-referential (equal to taxon_ID) for already-accepted rows, not NA – this is what lets update_taxa() resolve a matched name forward to its current accepted name regardless of whether it matched an accepted name or a synonym. To map a table with other column names onto this format interactively, see taxonAlign.dataprep::build_taxonomic_reference().

taxon_ranks_to_check

Optional character vector restricting which taxonomic ranks (besides species/infraspecific ranks) are retained in the returned resources for higher-rank matching (e.g. c("genus", "family")). Defaults to NULL, which keeps every rank present in taxonomic_resources.

Value

A named list of tibbles (and, for species, a further named list split by taxonomic_status): one element per taxonomic rank present in taxonomic_resources (after applying taxon_ranks_to_check, if supplied), plus subgenus_v2 when subgenus-rank rows are present (see Details).

Details

Unlike APCalign's load_taxonomic_resources(), which only ever assembles the fixed APC/APNI combination, this function works on whatever combined reference data the user supplies – at whatever set of taxonomic ranks it happens to contain, not just genus/species/family.

Column names are normalised on the way in, exactly the way APCalign::load_taxonomic_resources() normalises APC/APNI's raw Darwin Core column names to its own convention – e.g. a raw canonicalName/taxonRank/taxonomicStatus/scientificName column is renamed to canonical_name/taxon_rank/taxonomic_status/scientific_name. This keeps canonical_name the only name field taxonAlign ever refers to.

When multiple tables are supplied, whichever is supplied first is preferred when a name exists in more than one, whatever taxonomic status each gives it. Within one table, a name listed more than once is matched to its most reliable status first (accepted, then the various kinds of synonym, then misapplications, ...).

Two matching conventions for subgenus names are supported side by side: some input name lists write the subgenus alone (e.g. "Podosemum"), others write the Genus (Subgenus) bracketed convention (e.g. "Boronia (Podosemum)"). To support both, when taxonomic_resources contains subgenus-rank rows, resources$subgenus holds the plain subgenus names (used for the first convention) and resources$subgenus_v2 additionally holds a genus_and_subgenus column (used for the second).

Examples

reference <- data.frame(
  canonical_name = c("Boronia", "Boronia serrulata", "Boronia oldname"),
  scientific_name = c("Boronia Sm.", "Boronia serrulata Sm.", "Boronia oldname Sm."),
  taxon_rank = c("genus", "species", "species"),
  taxonomic_status = c("accepted", "accepted", "synonym"),
  taxonomic_dataset = "MY_LIST", genus = "Boronia",
  taxon_ID = c("1", "2", "3"), accepted_name_usage_ID = c("1", "2", "2")
)
# prepare once, then reuse for several lookups
resources <- prepare_taxonomic_resources(reference)
names(resources)
#> [1] "species" "genus"  
align_taxa("Boronia serulata", resources)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 12
#>   original_name    identifier cleaned_name     aligned_name    taxonomic_dataset
#>   <chr>            <chr>      <chr>            <chr>           <chr>            
#> 1 Boronia serulata NA         Boronia serulata Boronia serrul… MY_LIST          
#> # ℹ 7 more variables: taxon_rank <chr>, taxonomic_status <chr>, taxon_ID <chr>,
#> #   accepted_name_usage_ID <chr>, aligned_reason <chr>, alignment_code <chr>,
#> #   chars_changed <int>
